A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NSReg research work. All 22 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original graph anomaly detection experiments, regularisation ablations, sensitivity studies and runtime/resource measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains original detection, ablation and sensitivity results and reports additional baseline evaluations in Table 1.

M1.justification: The three relation types, normality labels, representation architecture, regularisation objective, training procedure and inference pipeline remain unchanged. Section 3 expands explanations without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Photo, Computers, CS, Yelp, ogbn-arxiv, ogbn-proteins and T-Finance under the same open-set scenarios. T-Finance anomaly clustering receives additional main-text mention in v4 but was already documented in v3 Appendix B.2.2.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds OCGNN, CONDA (the table's spelling) and ADA-GAD to the 13 retained comparators. ADA-GAD has results on three datasets and an out-of-memory entry for Yelp. The supervised accuracy comparisons remain unchanged; the separate runtime comparison is removed.

E3.justification: Removing v3 Appendix C.3 eliminates the supplementary evaluation of average training time and peak VRAM. Detection metrics, class rotation, preprocessing, labelled-data budgets and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 removes the runtime/resource analysis testing NSR's training overhead and efficiency relative to competing methods. The regulariser ablations, normal-anomaly relation experiment, hyperparameter sensitivity and data-efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both specify five random runs, averaging across anomaly-class rotations, and mean±standard-deviation reporting. The additional baseline rows follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds baseline results, including average all-anomaly AUC-ROC of 0.496 for OCGNN and 0.441 for CONDA. Retained detection values and plotted results are unchanged; NSReg's corresponding all/unseen averages remain 0.849/0.808. v3 Table 10's timing and memory results disappear.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 retains its assumptions and conclusion, and Appendix A retains the same contradiction proof. Explicitly writing the mapping composition, explaining the existing normal-region equivalence and repairing notation do not introduce substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The supervised open-set problem, normal-structure regularisation contribution, plugin applicability and unseen-anomaly generalisation claims remain the same. The 14%/10% headline advantages added to v4's abstract were already claimed in v3's introduction.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly excludes unsupervised use, adds a rationale against injected-anomaly benchmarks based on possible information leakage, and clarifies normality alignment. It removes the runtime/scalability interpretation alongside the resource analysis. The immediate-neighbourhood limitation remains, with sampling or approximation suggested as future work.

D1.justification: The runtime-section deletion removes the NVIDIA A100 and 28 AMD EPYC 7663 CPU-core disclosure, together with measured resource requirements. Appendix B retains the dependency versions, preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters and pseudocode.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for OCGNN, the contrastive augmentation baseline, ADA-GAD, GADBench and a recent graph anomaly detection survey. Prior work additionally supports the benchmark-selection rationale, while the main related-work categories and contribution positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites refine the abstract, introduction, theoretical exposition, dataset rationale and limitations. Terminology and cross-references are corrected, while the main narrative and section sequence remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 substantially reformats the document's title, headings, recurring headers and references, and rearranges or resizes multiple figures and tables. Tables 2–3 and Figure 4/Table 4 become adjacent displays, and Figures 8–9 share one page. Table 1 expands and the runtime table disappears; all nine figures retain their contents.

improvement.justification: v4 broadens baseline coverage and clarifies applicability and benchmark rationale, but removes the only runtime/VRAM comparison and its hardware documentation. The method, proof and retained detection results are unchanged. These gains in comparison breadth and explanation trade against reduced practical evaluability, without a reliably assessable net quality direction.
